Create a rulebook

Source: R/rulebook.R
rulebook.Rd

A rulebook holds every planning rule for one plan (or one scenario of it), with a citation for every value. Build it with the add_*() and set_*() functions, or read it from a file with read_rulebook().

Usage

rulebook(
  name,
  id = NULL,
  jurisdiction = NULL,
  country = NULL,
  effective_date = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  units = c("m", "ft"),
  hemisphere = NULL
)

Arguments

name

Name of the plan.

id

Short identifier, e.g. "wcc-dp-2024".

jurisdiction

Council, city or state.

country

ISO country code.

effective_date

Date the rules are as at ("YYYY-MM-DD").

source

Where the rules were read from.

units

"m" (default) or "ft": units of every length and area in the rulebook. Results are always computed in metres.

hemisphere

"south" or "north", for rules that depend on which way a boundary faces. If NULL it is inferred from the data at run time.

Value

A plancap_rulebook.

Examples

rb <- rulebook("Exampleton District Plan", id = "exampleton-dp",
               jurisdiction = "Exampleton", country = "NZ")
rb <- add_zone(rb, zone("LDR", "Low Density Residential",
  height = height_limit(8, source = "LDR-S1"),
  setbacks = list(yard(3, "road", source = "LDR-S2")),
  coverage = ratio(0.35, source = "LDR-S3")))
rb
#> <plancap rulebook> Exampleton District Plan
#> exampleton-dp | Exampleton | NZ
#> 1 zone, 0 overlays, 0 areas, 0 bonuses, 0 entitlements; 0 unmodelled rules.
#> Units: metres.
#>  zone label                   method     height setbacks coverage codes
#>  LDR  Low Density Residential volumetric 8      1        0.35     LDR
